pass_a_gloss: Tome 5. [Lemma, Isaiah 40:15-21:] If all the nations were reckoned as a drop from a jar, and as a tipping of a scale, and will be reckoned as spittle? And Lebanon is not sufficient for burning, and all the four-footed are not sufficient for whole burnt offering, and all the nations are for nothing, and were reckoned as nothing. To whom did you liken the Lord, and to what likeness did you liken him? Did a carpenter make an image, or did a goldsmith, having melted gold, gild him around? For a carpenter chooses unrotting wood, and wisely seeks how he will set up his image, so that it may not be shaken. Will you not know? Do you not hear? Was it not announced to you from beginning? Did you not know the foundations of the earth? The prophetic word having recalled for us the economy with flesh of the Only-Begotten, and having sufficiently marvelled at the ineffable wisdom, through which we both have been saved, and, having come to know the Master by nature and truly, have been deemed worthy of the grace from him, gathered as lambs by his arm, and having come to be under him as under a shepherd very good; for he laid down the life for his own sheep. And indeed having shown the Mind to be out of reach of being able to see, or perhaps to measure, and having confessed him to be the highest wisdom and beyond all things, he necessarily brought in the one making words to those from the nations, or those still worshipping the creation beside the one who created, and carrying them away from the ancient and ancestral and father-handed error, and moving them to the better things and bringing them back to the knowledge befitting man. He shows then the measureless pre-eminence of the God who rules all, and the surpassing dignity of the majesty in him, and that all things are small to him, and would be reckoned in equal [measure] with nothing, as compared, I mean, with the exceeding greatness of the power and glory in him. For this reason he says: If all the nations were reckoned as a drop from a jar and as a tipping of a scale, and will be reckoned as spittle. And these are small and wholly worth nothing. For what is one drop falling from a jar? And what would be the tipping of a scale, bringing toward equality the side that seems defeated? And what is spittle, that is, the human spit? But Lebanon would not suffice for him at all, he says, for burning, or all the four-footed for whole burnt offering. And such things are wholly contemptible; even if all were brought for whole burnt offering to him [the section breaks off].
pass_b_english: “All the nations are counted as a drop from a jar and as the tipping of a scale, and they will be counted as spittle. Lebanon is not enough for burning, and all the four-footed beasts are not enough for a whole burnt offering, and all the nations are nothing and have been counted as nothing. To whom have you likened the Lord, and with what likeness have you likened Him? Did a carpenter make an image, or did a goldsmith melt gold and gild it over? For the carpenter chooses wood that does not rot, and wisely seeks how he will set up his image so that it may not totter. Will you not know? Do you not hear? Has it not been told to you from the beginning? Have you not known the foundations of the earth?” (Isaiah 40:15-21).

The prophetic word has recalled for us the dispensation of the Only-begotten in the flesh, and has marvelled fittingly at the ineffable wisdom through which we have been saved and, having come to know Him who is Master by nature and in truth, have been counted worthy of His grace: gathered like lambs by His arm (Isaiah 40:11), and placed under Him as under a Shepherd exceedingly good, for He laid down His life for His own sheep (John 10:11). It has also shown that the Mind is beyond our reach, whether to see or even perhaps to measure (Isaiah 40:13), and has confessed Him to be the highest Wisdom, beyond all things. So it has of necessity brought in one who addresses those from the nations, that is, those who still worship the creation rather than the Creator (Romans 1:25); he takes them away from their ancient error, the error of their forebears handed down from their fathers, moves them to better things, and brings them back to the knowledge that befits human beings.

He therefore shows the measureless pre-eminence of God, who rules all things, and the surpassing dignity of the majesty that is in Him, and that all things are small to Him and would be reckoned as equal to nothing when set beside, I mean, the exceeding greatness of His power and glory. That is why he says: “All the nations are counted as a drop from a jar and as the tipping of a scale, and they will be counted as spittle.” These things are small and worth nothing at all. For what is one drop falling from a jar? And what would the tipping of a scale be, which brings the side that seems lighter up to an even balance? And what is spittle, that is, the spit of a man?

But Lebanon, he says, would not be enough for Him for burning, nor all the four-footed beasts for a whole burnt offering. Such things are wholly contemptible; even if all of them were brought to Him for a whole burnt offering …

choices.english: the dispensation of the Only-begotten in the flesh
choices.why: οἰκονομία names the saving plan of the Incarnation.

choices.english: the Mind is beyond our reach
choices.why: Isaiah 40:13 'who has known the mind of the Lord'; Cyril means God's Mind, capitalised.

choices.english: the error of their forebears handed down from their fathers

choices.why: Cyril explains it as the small weight that brings the lighter side level.

choices.english: the knowledge that befits human beings
choices.why: True knowledge of God is what fits rational human nature.
